title: Permission Slip for the Apple Orchard
text:
Dear Families,

On Friday, our class will visit Happy Hills Apple Orchard. We will leave at nine o'clock and come back before lunch. Students will pick apples, pet a {adjective} goat, and ride on a wagon pulled by a {noun}. The farmer will teach us how to {verb} like a real apple picker.

Please send your child with a sack lunch, a water bottle, and {number} {plural noun}. Students should wear comfy shoes. Last year someone wore {plural noun}, and they got very muddy. We need three grown-up helpers. Helpers must be able to walk {adverb}, count to twenty, and carry a {adjective} basket.

Please sign below and return this slip by Wednesday.

My child may go on the field trip. I promise to pack something {adjective} for lunch. I will remind my child not to {verb} on the bus.

Grown-up signature: {name}
Favorite kind of apple: {color} and {adjective}

title: What to Pack for the Aquarium
text:
Our class is going to the City Aquarium on Tuesday! Here is your packing list.

A lunch box with a sandwich, a juice box, and a small bag of {plural noun}. A raincoat, because the dolphins like to {verb} at the front row. A notebook for drawing your favorite {noun}. A {adjective} hat so your teacher can find you. One stuffed {animal} for the bus ride. Only one, please. The bus is very full.

Things NOT to pack: fishing poles, buckets, or {plural noun}. The sea turtles get {adjective} when they see those. Also, please leave your {noun} at home. The octopus always tries to borrow one.

We will walk {adverb} through the glass tunnel where fish swim over your head. Hold your buddy's {body part} and keep {verb ending in ing}. Our bus leaves at {number} o'clock sharp. Please do not be {adjective}!

title: Bus Rules for Field Trip Day
text:
Welcome aboard Bus Number 4! My name is Miss Dot, and I will be your driver today. Please listen to these rules.

Rule one: Stay in your seat. The seats are soft and {adjective}, so this should be easy. Rule two: Use your inside voice. If you must sing, please sing {adverb}. Songs about {plural noun} are allowed. Rule three: Keep your hands and your {body part} inside the bus at all times.

Rule four: Do not {verb} in the aisle. The aisle is only for walking and for my lunch {noun}. Rule five: If you see a {animal} out the window, you may wave. Last week we saw one, and it {past tense verb} back. Rule six: No {verb ending in ing} until we get to the museum. Rule seven: Snacks stay in your bag. That means crackers, apples, and especially {plural noun}.

If everyone follows the rules, we will play my favorite game: Spot the {adjective} {noun}. Everyone who plays gets a {color} sticker!

title: Dear Diary, We Went to the Farm
text:
Dear Diary,

Today our class went to Sunny Acres Farm. The bus ride took {number} minutes. First we saw a big red barn. Inside, a cow named Daisy was eating {plural noun}. The farmer said Daisy is the most {adjective} cow in the whole state.

Then we got to milk a goat. I was nervous, but I did it {adverb}. The goat looked at me and {past tense verb}. I think that means she liked me. After lunch we went on a hayride and sang songs about {plural noun}. My friend Priya found a feather that looked just like a {noun}. The farmer said, "Please do not {verb} near the pigs."

At the gift shop, I bought a {adjective} pencil for my little brother. The farmer gave everyone a jar of {adjective} honey. On the way home, everyone fell asleep except our teacher. She was still {verb ending in ing}. Tomorrow I will ask Mom if we can keep a {animal} in the {noun}.

title: Postcard from the Science Museum
text:
Dear Grandpa,

Greetings from the Science Museum! I am writing this postcard on the bus. The first room had a giant model of a {noun}. It was as tall as a {animal}! A man in a white coat showed us how to make it {verb}. Next was the dinosaur room. The sign said this dinosaur liked to eat {plural noun} and nap in the sun. It must have been very {adjective}.

My favorite part was the bubble room. I made a bubble so big that my whole {body part} fit inside. My teacher {past tense verb} when she saw it. In the space room, you can push a button and hear what {plural noun} sound like on Mars.

I got you a {adjective} magnet at the gift shop. It is shaped like a {noun} and says "{silly word}" on it. I will tell you everything very {adverb}.

Love,
Rosie

P.S. Please tell Grandma I learned how to {verb}!

title: Welcome to the Town History Museum
text:
Hello, students, and welcome to the Town History Museum! My name is Mr. Pickett, and I will be your tour guide. Please stay with your group and walk {adverb}.

In this first room, you can see an old wagon. People used wagons to carry flour, wood, and {plural noun} into town. This one was pulled by a {adjective} horse named Clover. Over here is a schoolroom from long ago. Children wrote on tiny chalkboards and learned how to {verb}. Good students got a {noun} to take home. Please do not {verb} on the old desks.

This glass case holds the town's first mail bag. Inside, we found a letter that said, "Dear Mabel, please send more {plural noun}." And here is the giant clock. Every hour, a little wooden {animal} pops out and starts {verb ending in ing}. Last week, it {past tense verb} for a whole hour.

Today everything in the gift shop costs {number} pennies. Please wipe your {plural noun} on the way out. Thank you for being such {adjective} visitors!

title: Thank You, Zookeeper Jo
text:
Dear Zookeeper Jo,

Thank you for showing our class around the zoo last week. We had a {adjective} time. Our favorite part was watching the giraffes eat breakfast. We did not know that giraffes like {plural noun} so much. When you fed them, they {past tense verb} with joy. Thank you for letting us touch the turtle's shell. It felt bumpy and {adjective}, like a {noun}.

We also loved the penguins. They walk {adverb} and look like they are wearing tiny {plural noun}. Some of us tried to {verb} like penguins all the way back to the bus. Our teacher said that was very {adjective}.

When we visit in the spring, we will bring you some {food} as a thank-you gift. We hope the lion is still {verb ending in ing} when we get there.

From,
Room 14

P.S. Benji wants to know if the zoo has a {silly word} and a {animal}.

title: Our Day at the Fire Station
text:
Here is our schedule for the field trip to Fire Station 5.

8:30: Get on the bus. Find your buddy and sit {adverb}. 9:00: Arrive at the fire station. Firefighter Lopez will meet us with her dog, Sparky. Sparky is very {adjective} and loves to be patted. Last year, Sparky {past tense verb} on the fire truck all day. 9:15: Tour the fire truck. The truck has ladders, hoses, and a special box full of {plural noun}. We will all get to ring the bell {number} times.

10:00: Firefighter Lopez will teach us how to {verb} like a firefighter. 10:30: Try on a real helmet. It is heavy and smells a little bit like {food}. 11:00: Snack time in the kitchen. Today the firefighters are making {adjective} pancakes with {plural noun} on top.

11:30: Say goodbye. Each student will get a {color} sticker and a picture of a {noun}. Sparky will wave goodbye with his {body part}. 12:00: Ride back to school. Please keep {verb ending in ing} quietly in your seat.

title: Instructions for Field Trip Helpers
text:
Thank you for helping on our trip to the Children's Garden! Here is what every grown-up helper should know.

You will be in charge of {number} students. Please count them every time you walk through a gate. They will try to {verb}, but stay calm. Your group is called the {adjective} {plural noun}. Please cheer your group name loudly at lunch.

Remind students to smell the flowers {adverb} and not to pick them. The roses are very {adjective} this time of year. The ducks in the pond are friendly, but they really like {plural noun}. If a duck follows you, just keep walking and smile. Never feed the ducks after {number} o'clock.

At noon, we will meet under the big {noun} for lunch. You may sit on a blanket or on a {noun}. If a child asks a question you cannot answer, just say, "Let's ask the {adjective} gardener!" Everyone must wash their {body part} before snack time.

Thank you for {verb ending in ing} with us today!

title: Kid News Visits the Bakery
text:
This is Channel 2 Kid News with a special report.

Today, Mrs. Hart's second grade class took a field trip to Sugar Moon Bakery. The baker, Mr. Flores, was already {verb ending in ing} when the class arrived. First, the students washed their {plural noun} and put on paper hats. Then they learned how to {verb} like real bakers. Mr. Flores says the trick is to push the dough {adverb} and sing to it.

Next, the class made cupcakes. Each student added sprinkles and one {adjective} {noun} on top. Mr. Flores said it was the most {adjective} batch he had ever seen. Then the big oven beeped. Out came {number} loaves of bread shaped like {plural noun}. The whole class {past tense verb} and clapped.

Every student went home with a cookie and a recipe for {food} muffins. Next year, the class hopes to visit a {noun} factory. Back to you in the studio, {name}!
